manifest.name: Ops / Incident Runbook
manifest.description: Incident response pipeline: alerts / triaging / mitigating / resolved / postmortem kanban. Team: on-call and escalation leads. Ceremonies: incident open, postmortem.
manifest.author: Squadboard Team

team.name: OnCall
team.charter:
# OnCall

## Role
On-Call Lead — first responder, owns incident triage, mitigation, and resolution.

## Expertise
- Incident classification (SEV1–SEV4)
- Runbook execution
- Stakeholder communication
- Rapid mitigation strategies

## Style
Calm under pressure. Communicate status every 15 minutes during active incidents. No assumption is too basic to check.

team.name: Escalation
team.charter:
# Escalation

## Role
Escalation Lead — owns SEV1/SEV2 escalations, external communication, and postmortem facilitation.

## Expertise
- Severity escalation criteria
- Executive and customer communication
- Postmortem facilitation
- Blameless retrospective culture

## Style
Clear and accountable. Postmortems are about systems, not people.

ceremonies.name: Incident Open
ceremonies.workflowYaml:
name: Incident Open
steps:
  - type: agent_run
    label: OnCall declares and classifies incident
    agent: OnCall
    prompt: "Classify this incident: severity (SEV1 total outage / SEV2 major degradation / SEV3 minor impact / SEV4 no user impact), impacted services, impacted users (estimate), and initial hypothesis. Open the incident channel and page if SEV1/SEV2."
    timeout: 15m
  - type: agent_run
    label: OnCall applies runbook mitigations
    agent: OnCall
    prompt: "Apply the relevant runbook steps for this incident type. Document each action taken and its outcome. If no runbook exists, improvise and document your actions for later runbook creation. Update status every 15 minutes."
    timeout: 120m
  - type: agent_run
    label: OnCall writes resolution summary
    agent: OnCall
    prompt: "Write the resolution summary: what was the root cause, what mitigated it, when was full recovery, and what is the customer impact statement. Notify stakeholders."
    timeout: 20m

ceremonies.name: Postmortem
ceremonies.workflowYaml:
name: Postmortem
steps:
  - type: agent_run
    label: Escalation builds blameless timeline
    agent: Escalation
    prompt: "Build a blameless postmortem for this incident. Include: timeline (with timestamps), root cause (5 whys), contributing factors, detection gap (why did we not detect sooner?), response effectiveness, customer impact, and at least 3 action items with owners and due dates. Blameless means: identify system failures, not people failures."
    timeout: 60m
  - type: approve
    label: Postmortem review
    approvers: [OnCall]
    timeout: 48h
    timeoutAction: notify
  - type: agent_run
    label: File action items
    agent: Escalation
    prompt: "Convert each postmortem action item into a separate issue in this project. Each issue must have: description, owner, due date, and label 'postmortem-action'. Summarise the postmortem in the parent issue."
    timeout: 20m

skills.name: Incident Timeline Builder
skills.description: Structured incident timeline: timestamped events, detection, impact windows, mitigation steps, resolution.
skills.promptAddendum:
## Incident Timeline Format

Every incident timeline must follow this structure:

```
**Incident:** <title>
**Severity:** SEV1 / SEV2 / SEV3 / SEV4
**Duration:** <start time> → <end time> (<total duration>)
**Customer impact:** <affected users/services and impact description>

### Timeline
| Time (UTC) | Event |
|------------|-------|
| HH:MM      | Alert fired: <alert name> |
| HH:MM      | OnCall acknowledged |
| HH:MM      | Incident declared SEV<N> |
| HH:MM      | <mitigation action taken> |
| HH:MM      | Partial recovery: <what recovered> |
| HH:MM      | Full recovery confirmed |
| HH:MM      | Incident closed |

### Detection gap
<How long between first symptom and alert? Why?>

### Root cause
<5-whys chain>

### Action items
| # | Action | Owner | Due |
|---|--------|-------|-----|
| 1 | ...    | ...   | ... |
```

Rules:
- All timestamps in UTC. Never use local time.
- Detection gap analysis is mandatory — if we caught it fast, explain why.
- Root cause must be a system failure, not a person mistake.

routing.rawRule: | sev1 | Escalation | SEV1 incidents escalate immediately. |
| sev2 | Escalation | SEV2 incidents route to Escalation. |
| incident | OnCall | Incidents route to OnCall for initial triage. |
| postmortem-action | OnCall | Postmortem action items route to OnCall. |
| * | OnCall | All unmatched alerts route to OnCall. |
